title: Fuel — Boost Pumps — Installation of the Coarser Inlet Filter Element
abstract: Replacement of the 40 micron boost pump inlet filter by a 74 micron element in a longer housing, removing the low pressure advisories seen on aircraft uplifting sustainable aviation fuel blends.

sections.planning_reason: Operators uplifting sustainable aviation fuel blends reported low pressure advisories on the inner boost pumps, typically two to four sectors after a blend uplift and clearing once the tank had been run down. Twenty-nine advisories were logged across the fleet in eighteen months and eleven pumps were removed, nine of which tested serviceable in the shop. The filter deposit is a soft gel consistent with trace polar compounds in some blends, sitting on a mesh finer than the pump requires. Operators planning to increase their blend ratio should embody this Service Bulletin first.
sections.description: The 40 micron inlet filter element is replaced by a 74 micron element that is 18 mm longer, in a replacement housing sized to take it. The downstream pressure regulator is re-shimmed so that the differential pressure switch trips at the same delta as before. The pump, the pump inlet duct and the tank plumbing are unchanged.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Defuel and purge the affected tank and make it safe for entry. Open the tank access panels in zones 591 and 691. Do the removal task AMM-M-28-20-11-000-006-A for the inlet filter assembly. Remove the existing housing and clean the mounting face. Install the replacement housing D2820117143540 with the longer element and close it with self-locking nuts EN968165-23. Re-shim the pressure regulator D2820116810419 to the dimension in the accomplishment instructions and check the differential pressure switch trip point on the test rig. Do a leak check at operating pressure. Close the tank, refuel and do a boost pump functional test including the pump 41QA output check. Record the embodiment and update the filter replacement interval in the maintenance programme.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00373 that are still pre MOD-163011. Aircraft from the production cut-in onward already carry the coarser element. The longer element will not fit the pre-modification housing, so the housing and the element must be changed together.
sections.material_note: Kit K2820-1095-01 contains four housings, four elements and the nut set for one aircraft. Lead time is twenty weeks and the housing is the long-lead item. The removed housings are not returnable. Because a tank entry is required, operators are strongly advised to combine this Service Bulletin with any other scheduled tank work.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled tank entry, or within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
